name: fix108_slope_ground
verifies: fix-108 [owner, Demo_2026-10-18c]: deer on a mountain slope floated / stood on cliff faces as if without gravity. A deer and a wolf on the ~42° slope at (497.1, 109.06, -44.6) (G3Cli collision column: 0.77 m/m in x, 0.5 m/m in z) stand with their feet on the collision floor (|gap| <= 5 cm) idle and walking across it; a deer put on the 65° face at (495.1, 106.46, -44.6) beside Deer#bb7c728e's G3 spawn (494.96, 105.97, -45.28: 67°) slides down onto walkable floor (G3 slide mode beyond SteepGroundAngleMax 49°); the fix-99 cave floor is still the floor under the Reddock cave roof
steps: spawn Deer attitude=neutral near=497.1,109.06,-44.6 dist=0.5 as=d
spawn Wolf attitude=neutral near=498.1,109.83,-44.6 dist=0.5 as=w
spawn Deer attitude=neutral near=706.52,33.9,-77.06 dist=0.5 as=c
notes: Foot gap = feet height minus the collision surface nearest them in the column under the body's origin (its own ray, ScenarioRunner.Fix108 NpcFootGap). G3 PutToGround puts a body on the floor of a vertical ray under its origin and does not tilt animals, so on a slope a long body's downhill legs hang over the ground by about half its length x tan(slope) also in G3; what made the deer look weightless were bodies kept on 60-70° faces (spawned there, wandered up them: no slope limit off the NavMesh) and heights from a NavMesh point or the spawn's height. Rules: G3.Player.NpcGroundRules (tests NpcGroundRulesTests).
